title: Finite projective cohomology splitting and shifted-free derived maps
statement:
Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Assume evaluation at $U$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. Let $C$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and use module sheaves and their unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(C))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $N$ be an object of this category. Fix integers $a\leq b$, assume $H^q(N)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$, and choose finite integers $r_q\geq0$ and isomorphisms $\theta_q:C^{\oplus r_q}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(N)$ for $a\leq q\leq b$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $Z^\bullet$ be any complex representing $N$. The zero-differential complex $V^\bullet$ with $V^q=C^{\oplus r_q}$ in $[a,b]$ and zero terms elsewhere admits a chain map $V^\bullet\to Z^\bullet$ inducing exactly the chosen $\theta_q$ on cohomology; in particular it is a quasi-isomorphism. For every $A\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(C))$, every $q\in\mathbf Z$ and every finite $r$, the map taking the images of the standard generators induces a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}(C))}(C^{\oplus r}[-q],A)\cong H^q(A)(U)^r.$$
For every bounded-above complex $P^\bullet$ of projective $C$-module sheaves (projective means having the lifting property along epimorphisms), derived morphisms from $P^\bullet$ to any complex are represented by chain maps, uniquely up to chain homotopy, where $f-g=dh+hd$ defines chain homotopy. Consequently a morphism $C^{\oplus r_b}[-b]\to N$ inducing $\theta_b$ is, under the displayed $V^\bullet\cong N$, exactly the inclusion of its degree-$b$ summand.

proof.text: Evaluation on $U$ takes epimorphisms of $C$-module sheaves to surjections. Indeed the exact forgetful functor of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] takes such an epimorphism to an epimorphism of abelian sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] its underlying map is locally surjective; by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] it is therefore an epimorphism of sheaves of sets. Apply the hypothesis on evaluation at $U$. The small pro-etale site has sheafification in an ambient universe containing the site and coefficients, as required by the forgetful result. Kernels are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus evaluation preserves kernels and is surjective on every module-sheaf quotient.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; Tag 03CN, lemma-abelian-abelian (5); literature/stacks-project/sites.tex, Tag 00WN, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves.

proof.text: The object $U\xrightarrow{1}U$ is terminal in its small pro-etale site. For every module sheaf $F$, a map $C^{\oplus r}\to F$ is uniquely specified by $r$ sections $s_j\in F(U)$: on $T\to U$ its formula is $(c_j)_j\mapsto\sum_jc_j(s_j|_T)$. Semilinear restrictions in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] show these formulas commute with restriction, and linearity shows every map has this formula. Finite direct sums here are the sectionwise finite products of modules, which satisfy the sheaf condition coordinatewise. Given an epimorphism $F\to G$ and a map $C^{\oplus r}\to G$, step 1 lifts each of its finitely many generator sections to $F(U)$; the displayed formula gives a lift of the map. Hence every $C^{\oplus r}$ is a projective object. For $r=0$ both the map and the lift are unique.

proof.text: For each $q\in[a,b]$, put $\mathcal Z^q=\ker(d_Z^q)$, and let $p_q:\mathcal Z^q\twoheadrightarrow H^q(Z)$ be the quotient by $\operatorname{im}(d_Z^{q-1})$, using [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Regard $\theta_q$ as a map to $H^q(Z)$ via the fixed identification of $Z$ with a representative of $N$. Projectivity from step 2 gives $t_q:C^{\oplus r_q}\to\mathcal Z^q$ with $p_qt_q=\theta_q$. Define $v^q:V^q\to Z^q$ as $t_q$ followed by the kernel inclusion and define it to be zero outside $[a,b]$. Since $d_Z^qv^q=0$ and $d_V=0$, these maps form a chain map. Its cohomology map in degree $q$ is exactly $p_qt_q=\theta_q$; outside the interval both cohomology sheaves vanish. Thus $v$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and its image in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is the asserted isomorphism $V\cong N$.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, lifting rho to tilde rho: apply the lifting separately to the chosen bases in each of the finitely many degrees.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] in the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(C)$ of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Every bounded-above complex of projective module sheaves is K-projective. In the Hom-complex description of K-projectivity, degree-zero cycles are chain maps and degree-zero boundaries are maps $d_Eh+hd_P$; thus acyclicity implies precisely the null-homotopy condition used by the next node. Then [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] identifies its morphisms in the homotopy category with its morphisms in the unbounded derived category. By that node's definition, the homotopy category has chain maps modulo $f-g=d_Eh+hd_P$. This proves the chain-map representative assertion and its uniqueness precisely up to the homotopy in the statement. This argument does not require enough projective objects or any boundedness of the target.

Fix a representative $E$ of $A$ and put $S=C^{\oplus r}[-q]$, the single-term complex in degree $q$. It is bounded above and projective by step 2, so step 4 applies. A chain map $S\to E$ is exactly a tuple of cycles $z_j\in\ker(d_E^q)(U)$ by the generator formula of step 2. Two such maps are homotopic exactly when their cycle differences have the form $d_E^{q-1}(h_j)$ for sections $h_j\in E^{q-1}(U)$: the only possibly nonzero homotopy component is $S^q\to E^{q-1}$, and $d_S=0$. Write $\mathcal B^q=\operatorname{im}(d_E^{q-1})$. Step 1 applied to $E^{q-1}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B^q$ and to $\ker(d_E^q)\twoheadrightarrow H^q(E)$ gives
$$H^q(E)(U)=\ker(d_E^q)(U)/d_E^{q-1}(E^{q-1}(U)).$$
Thus the homotopy classes, and hence the derived morphisms, are naturally $H^q(A)(U)^r$. The map sends a derived arrow to its cohomology map on the global standard generators, so it is independent of the representative $E$ by [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For a derived arrow $\alpha:A\to A'$, functoriality of $H^q$ gives $H^q(\alpha\circ f)(e_j)=H^q(\alpha)(H^q(f)(e_j))$; this proves naturality for all derived arrows, including those not represented by chain maps between these representatives.

source.place: Tag 064B, lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex, with the explicit cycle and boundary calculation; literature/stacks-project/proetale.tex, Tag 09C3, lifting the rho(e_s).

proof.text: Let $\iota_b:C^{\oplus r_b}[-b]\to V$ be the inclusion in degree $b$, with all other components zero. The composite $v\iota_b:C^{\oplus r_b}[-b]\to N$ induces $\theta_b$ by step 3. Any other derived morphism inducing $\theta_b$ has the same tuple of standard-generator cohomology sections, hence equals $v\iota_b$ by step 5. Composing with $v^{-1}$ identifies it with $\iota_b$. The construction also covers $a=b$, a zero top rank, all ranks zero, and the empty scheme: no nonempty set of generators is required when the relevant free object is zero.

Step 1: the forgetful node's clause (1) gives exactness, then abelian epi = locally surjective = set-sheaf epi, then the evaluation hypothesis. The site is V-small, so sheafification exists. Step 2: id_U is terminal, so Hom(C^r,F)=F(U)^r and C^r is projective. Step 3: θ_q lifts along the epi from cycles onto H^q, and v is a quasi-iso without any boundedness of Z. Step 4: the Hom-complex form of K-projectivity in degree 0 is the null-homotopy form; Stacks 064B (derived.tex:6822) needs no enough projectives, and the Mathlib lemmas isKProjective_of_projective (KProjective.lean:111-124) and Qh_map_bijective (DerivedCategory/KProjective.lean:43-48) were read. Step 5: C^r[-q] sits in degree q, the only homotopy component is h^q, and step 1 gives H^q(E)(U)=ker(d^q)(U)/d(E^{q-1}(U)); the description f ↦ H^q(f)(e_j) gives representative independence and naturality. Step 6: uniqueness of the top inclusion follows from step 5. Edge cases checked: r=0, a=b, all ranks 0 (acyclic N), U empty, one-point site. Tags 09C3, 064B, 03DA, 03CN and 00WN confirmed in Stacks.
